summary: The paper proves a lifting theorem for G-valued residual representations ρ̄ : Γ_F → G(k) of global fields, reducible ones included (Theorem 5.2 = Theorem E): under Assumptions 3.1, 4.1, 5.1 (vanishing of H¹(Gal(K/F), ρ̄(𝔤^der)^*), H⁰ conditions, no common subquotients of ρ̄(𝔤^der) and ρ̄(𝔤^der)^*, local lifts) and oddness over totally real F, ρ̄ has a geometric lift with image containing Ĝ^der(O′) and prescribed local components. The method refines the authors' earlier relative deformation theory (FKP19) with a new doubling argument built on cyclic submodules and auxiliary primes t_b, t_0, so ρ̄(𝔤^der) need not be semisimple; §6 treats residually split ρ̄. Applications: every odd reducible ρ̄ : Γ_ℚ → GL_2(k), p ≥ 3, with χ̄ ≠ κ̄^{−1} arises from a newform — the actual ρ̄, not its semisimplification (Theorem 7.4 = Theorem B, via Skinner–Wiles and Pan); automorphy of many reducible GL_n-valued ρ̄ over function fields via L. Lafforgue (Theorem 8.1, Corollaries 8.3 = Theorem C, 8.4); GSp_2n compatible systems (Proposition 9.1); group-theoretic criteria (Appendix A) and ordinary components of G-valued deformation rings (Appendix B). Nothing in the atlas plans Ramakrishna-style lifting, so the global theory and its applications become a Part II of GlobalGaloisDeformations; the G-valued local material is a source of LocalGaloisDeformationRings (R08.2, R08.6, L7), function-field duality a source of ArithmeticGaloisDuality, the BLGGT14 inputs a source of ModularityAndLanglandsExtensions ML.2, and the Allen–Newton–Thorne inputs join the proposed PolarizedAutomorphyLifting. Seven misprints are recorded.

items.name: A residual representation arising from a newform (lattice-sensitive)
items.statement: For an odd ρ̄ : Γ_ℚ → GL_2(k), k finite of characteristic p: ρ̄ arises from a newform f ∈ S_r(Γ_1(N)) (r ≥ 2) if, for E = E_{f,ι} the completion of ℚ(a_n(f)) at ι : E_f → ℚ̄_p with valuation ring O, there is a ρ_{f,ι}(Γ_ℚ)-stable lattice in E² whose integral model Γ_ℚ → GL_2(O), reduced along some O → k̄, is isomorphic to ρ̄. §7 (p. 35) calls ρ̄ : Γ_{ℚ,S} → GL_2(k) modular of weight r and level N when there are f ∈ S_r(Γ_1(N)), ι and an O_E-lattice inside ρ_{f,ι} with ρ̄_{f,ι} ≅ ρ̄ for some embedding O_E/m_E → k̄. The actual ρ̄, not its semisimplification, is to be matched.
items.locator: §1, p. 2 (diagram and definition); §7, p. 35 (modular of weight r and level N)
items.note: The atlas plans ρ_f (AutomorphicGaloisRepresentations R19.1), lattices and reduction followed by semisimplification (ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations R01.1) and Serre's statement for irreducible ρ̄, where the lattice is unique up to scaling; nothing plans the lattice-sensitive notion for residually reducible ρ_{f,ι}. Routed to the Part II's modularity layer.

items.name: Stable lattices of ρ_{f,ι} (Ribet, Serre)
items.statement: The semisimplification of the reduction of a ρ_{f,ι}(Γ_ℚ)-stable lattice in E² does not depend on the lattice. If ρ_{f,ι} is residually irreducible, the stable lattice is unique up to E^×. If ρ_{f,ι} is residually reducible, stable lattices are never unique up to scaling, but there are only finitely many up to scaling (ρ_{f,ι} being irreducible), and at least two non-isomorphic ρ̄ arise from f.
items.note: Independence of the semisimplification is planned in ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations R01.1 (Brauer–Nesbitt); the uniqueness and finiteness statements, and the existence of two non-isomorphic reductions, are not. They are the tree statements of the Bruhat–Tits item below; routed with it.

items.name: Theorem A (Hamblen–Ramakrishna 2008, Theorem 2)
items.statement: Let p ≥ 3, k finite of characteristic p, and ρ̄ : Γ_ℚ → GL_2(k) continuous and indecomposable with ρ̄ ∼ (χ̄ ∗; 0 1). Assume (1) χ̄(c) = −1, χ̄ ≠ κ̄^{±1}, χ̄² ≠ 1; (2) ρ̄|_{Γ_{ℚ_p}} is either ramified, or unramified but not of the form (1 ∗; 0 1); (3) k is spanned over 𝔽_p by the values of χ̄. Then ρ̄ arises from a newform of some level N and weight r ≥ 2.
items.note: Hamblen–Ramakrishna, Amer. J. Math. 130 (2008): lift ρ̄ to an ordinary geometric ρ with Hodge–Tate weights (r − 1, 0) and apply Skinner–Wiles. Assumptions (1) and (3) make ad(ρ̄) multiplicity-free with H¹(im ρ̄, ad ρ̄) = 0; (2) makes the local problem at p smooth and ρ distinguished at p (p. 3). Superseded by Theorem 7.4; recorded in the Part II as the statement it improves.

items.name: Conjecture D: lifting and automorphy of L-homomorphisms
items.statement: Let F be a global field of characteristic ≠ p, G′ quasi-split over F and G = ᴸG = G^∨ ⋊ Gal(F̃/F) its L-group over ℤ (F̃/F the smallest extension through which μ_{G′} factors [Bor79 §1.1]). Let S be finite, containing the primes ramified in F̃/F and, for F a number field, those above p, and ρ̄ : Γ_{F,S} → G(k) a continuous L-homomorphism; if F is a number field assume F totally real and ρ̄ odd. Then (1) there is a lift ρ : Γ_F → G(O), unramified outside a finite set, with Zariski-dense image and, for number fields, regular Hodge–Tate cocharacters; (2) there is an L-algebraic cuspidal π of G′(𝔸_F) such that one of the Galois representations ρ_{π,ι} conjecturally attached to (π, ι) [BG14, Conj. 3.2.2] is G^0(ℚ̄_p)-conjugate to ρ. If ρ̄|_{Γ_{F̃}} is absolutely irreducible, ρ and π can be taken unramified outside S.
items.locator: §1.1, Conjecture D, pp. 4–5, footnote 1 and the remark on p = 2
items.note: A conjecture, recorded as the target the lifting theorems give evidence for (Theorems B, C, E only when p ≫_G 0). Footnote 1: for G = G^0 with Zariski-dense image, Frobenius conjugacy classes determine the representation [BHKT19 Prop. 6.4]; over function fields ρ_{π,ι} is V. Lafforgue's. For p = 2 the paper suggests oddness should mean ρ̄(c_v) lifts to an order-2 η_v ∈ G(ℤ_p) with dim(𝔤^der_{ℚ̄_p})^{η_v=1} = dim Flag_{G^0}; even the trivial representation over a function field (G = GL_2) is outside the methods. Routed to the Part II's register of conditional statements.

items.name: Standing hypotheses on G, O and the multiplier
items.statement: G is a smooth group scheme over ℤ_p with G^0 split reductive and π_0(G) finite étale of order prime to p, satisfying [FKP19, Assumption 2.1]: p ≠ 2 is very good for G^der and the central isogeny G^der × Z^0_{G^0} → G^0 has kernel of order prime to p (implied by p ≫_G 0). O is the ring of integers of a finite E/ℚ_p with uniformiser ϖ and residue field k; F is a global field of characteristic prime to p. For ρ̄ : Γ_F → G(k), μ̄ : Γ_F → G/G^der(k) is its multiplier, and a lift μ : Γ_F → G/G^der(O) is fixed (de Rham above p for number fields); lifts are taken with multiplier μ (functors Lift^μ_ρ̄). Ĥ(O′) := ker(H(O′) → H(k′)) for a group scheme H over O and complete local O′ with residue field k′.
items.note: The atlas's global deformation theory is for GL_n and polarized groups (GlobalGaloisDeformations R04, G7, G8); the G-valued setting with disconnected G is new. FKP19 = Fakhruddin–Khare–Patrikis, Relative deformation theory, relative Selmer groups, and lifting irreducible Galois representations, Duke Math. J. 170 (2021), no. 16, not yet extracted (a prerequisite); the paper 'does not repeat from [FKP19] any of the local theory' (§1.4).

items.name: Local and global Galois cohomology over global function fields
items.statement: Tate local duality [NSW00, 7.2.6] and the local Euler characteristic formula [NSW00, 7.3.1] hold for local fields of characteristic ℓ > 0 with coefficients of order prime to ℓ. For F a global field, p ≠ char F, M a finite p-primary Γ_F-module and S containing the places where M ramifies (and, for number fields, the places above p and ∞): Poitou–Tate duality and its long exact sequence [NSW00, 8.6.7, 8.6.10], the Selmer variant from the proof of [NSW00, 8.7.9], and the Greenberg–Wiles formula [NSW00, 8.7.9] hold for Γ_{F,S}.
items.note: Number-field versions are planned: the global Euler characteristic in ArithmeticGaloisDuality R02.3, Poitou–Tate in R02.4 and the numerical Selmer bounds in R02.6. The function-field versions are not; they belong in those layers as their equal-characteristic cases.

items.name: Čebotarev density over global fields
items.statement: For a finite Galois extension of a global field F (number field or global function field), every conjugacy class of the Galois group is the Frobenius class of a set of places of positive density; for function fields see [FJ08, §6.4].
items.note: Number fields: Tau Ceti's Chebotarev roadmap, Layer 10 (Dirichlet-density Chebotarev; Tau Ceti already has frobeniusPrimeSet and the auxiliary-prime theorem NumberField.exists_auxiliaryPrime, but not the density theorem). Function fields: FunctionFieldArithmetic FA.5.

items.name: The tame quotient of a local Galois group, in both characteristics
items.statement: For a local field with residue field 𝔽 of characteristic prime to p, equal or mixed characteristic, the Galois group of the maximal tamely ramified extension with pro-p ramification index is ℤ_p ⋊ Ẑ, a generator σ of Ẑ acting by στσ^{−1} = τ^{#𝔽}; hence the analysis of local lifting rings at trivial primes [FKP19, §3] applies to function fields.
items.note: ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations R01.2 constructs tame characters and the ℓ ≠ p inertia structure for local fields of number fields; FunctionFieldArithmetic FA.3 plans ramification and inertia for positive-characteristic extensions.

items.name: Local lifting rings in equal characteristic
items.statement: For F a global function field, v a place and ρ̄ : Γ_{F_v} → G(k): the analysis of the generic fibre R^{□,μ}_ρ̄[1/ϖ] of [BG19, Theorem 3.3.3] (or [BP19, Theorem 14]) and [BG19, Lemma 3.4.1] hold, via Grothendieck's ℓ-adic monodromy theorem and Weil–Deligne representations; so for the Zariski closure R of an irreducible component of the generic fibre, [FKP19, Proposition 4.7] holds and R[1/ϖ] has an open dense regular subscheme (allowing [FKP19, Lemma 4.9]).
items.note: LocalGaloisDeformationRings R08.2 plans the GL_2 conditions away from p at places of number fields; the G-valued generic-fibre theorem of Bellovin–Gee (Algebra Number Theory 13 (2019)) and its equal-characteristic case are not planned. Routed as a source of R08.2.

items.name: Lemma 2.1: abelian extensions and the conjugation action
items.statement: Let L/F be a finite Galois extension and M/F abelian. Then Gal(L/F) acts trivially on Gal(LM/L) by the canonical action (σ·h = σ̃hσ̃^{−1} for any lift σ̃ ∈ Gal(LM/F)).
items.note: Elementary (restriction Gal(LM/L) → Gal(M/F) is injective and Gal(M/F) is abelian); used throughout without comment. Mathlib has the Galois correspondence but not this statement.

items.name: Assumption 3.1 and the fields K, F̃, K_∞
items.statement: Assume p ≫_G 0 and ρ̄ : Γ_{F,S} → G(k) continuous, unramified outside finite S (containing the places above p for number fields). Let F̃ be the smallest extension with ρ̄(Γ_{F̃}) ⊂ G^0(k), K = F(ρ̄, μ_p), and assume H¹(Gal(K/F), ρ̄(𝔤^der)^*) = 0. Fix a lift μ of μ̄; D is the largest integer with μ_{p^D} ⊂ K; K_∞ = K(μ_{p^∞}).
items.note: Hypothesis of the doubling method.

items.name: Definition 3.2: trivial primes
items.statement: A prime w of F is trivial if ρ̄|_{Γ_{F_w}} = 1 and N(w) ≡ 1 (mod p) (hence N(w) ≡ 1 mod p^D). Decomposition groups Γ_{F_v} ↪ Γ_F are fixed at the places of S and specified whenever auxiliary trivial primes are introduced, giving meaning to φ(σ_w), φ(τ_w) for φ ∈ H¹(Γ_{F,S′}, ρ̄(𝔤^der)) (Remark 3.3, [FKP19, Notation 5.1]).
items.note: FKP19 = Fakhruddin–Khare–Patrikis, Relative deformation theory, relative Selmer groups, and lifting irreducible Galois representations, Duke Math. J. 170 (2021), no. 16, not yet extracted (a prerequisite); the paper 'does not repeat from [FKP19] any of the local theory' (§1.4). Trivial primes and their local rings Lift^{μ,α} are [FKP19, §3].

items.name: Enlarging S to T: killing Ш¹_T(ρ̄(𝔤^der)^*)
items.statement: Enlarge S by trivial primes to T with Ш¹_T(Γ_{F,T}, ρ̄(𝔤^der)^*) = 0, hence Ш²_T(Γ_{F,T}, ρ̄(𝔤^der)) = 0. This uses Assumption 3.1: a non-zero ψ ∈ H¹(Γ_{F,S}, ρ̄(𝔤^der)^*) has ψ|_{Γ_K} ≠ 0, so some w split in K has ψ|_{Γ_{F_w}} ≠ 0. K_ψ ∩ K_∞ is K or K(μ_{p^{D+1}}), so N(w) ≡ 1 mod p^D and N(w) may be chosen non-trivial mod p^{D+1}.
items.note: As in [FKP19, §5].

items.name: Lemma 3.4(1)–(3): minimal Ш for cyclic submodules
items.statement: (1) There is a finite enlargement of T by trivial primes such that for every cyclic submodule M_Z = 𝔽_p[Γ_F]·Z ⊂ ρ̄(𝔤^der) (Z ∈ 𝔤^der), dim_{𝔽_p} Ш¹_T(Γ_{F,T}, M_Z^*) equals dim Ш¹_{T_max}(Γ_{F,T}, M_Z^*), T_max = S ∪ {all trivial primes}. (3) A further enlargement gives the same for the cyclic submodules M_λ = 𝔽_p[Γ_F]·λ ⊂ ρ̄(𝔤^der)^*.
items.note: Ш¹_T(M_Z^*) is finite-dimensional and there are finitely many M_Z^* (Remark 3.5: killing Ш outright would need H¹(Gal(K/F), M_Z^*) = 0 for all cyclic quotients).

items.name: Lemma 3.4(2): one new class ramified along Z
items.statement: For T as in Lemma 3.4(1) and a trivial prime w ∉ T, let L_{w,Z} ⊂ H¹(Γ_{F_w}, M_Z) be the cocycles with φ(τ_w) ∈ 𝔽_pZ. Then 0 → H¹(Γ_{F,T}, M_Z) → H¹_{L_{w,Z}}(Γ_{F,T∪w}, M_Z) —ev_{τ_w}→ 𝔽_pZ → 0 is exact (and likewise for M_λ ⊂ ρ̄(𝔤^der)^*).
items.note: Proof: the Greenberg–Wiles formula twice, the M_Z^* terms cancelling by (1).

items.name: The auxiliary primes t_b and t_0
items.statement: Fix a k-basis {e^*_b}_{b∈B} of ρ̄(𝔤^der)^*; add to T a trivial prime t_b for each b ∈ B and one more trivial prime t_0. They make the fixed fields of the auxiliary cocycles linearly disjoint, avoiding the field K′ of [FKP19, Definition 5.8].

items.name: Proposition 3.6 (first part): classes h^(v) spanning coker Ψ_T
items.statement: Let r = dim_{𝔽_p} coker(Ψ_T : H¹(Γ_{F,T}, ρ̄(𝔤^der)) → ⊕_{v∈T} H¹(Γ_{F_v}, ρ̄(𝔤^der))). Fix c ≥ D + 1 and a Galois L/F containing K, unramified outside T and linearly disjoint over K from K_∞ composed with any fields K_ψ, ψ ∈ H¹(Γ_{F,T}, ρ̄(𝔤^der)^*). There are Y_1, …, Y_r ∈ ⊕_{v∈T} H¹(Γ_{F_v}, ρ̄(𝔤^der)) mapping to an 𝔽_p-basis of coker Ψ_T and, for each i, q_i ∈ ker((ℤ/p^c)^× → (ℤ/p^D)^×) non-trivial mod p^{D+1}, a split maximal torus T_i, root α_i and root vector X_{α_i}, and (after choosing g_{L/K,i} ∈ Gal(L/K)) a Čebotarev set C_i of trivial primes v ∉ T with a positive upper-density subset l_i and classes h^(v) ∈ H¹(Γ_{F,T∪v}, ρ̄(𝔤^der)) for v ∈ l_i, such that N(v) ≡ q_i (mod p^c) and σ_v ↦ g_{L/K,i} for v ∈ C_i, and for v ∈ l_i: h^(v)|_T = Y_i; h^(v)(τ_v) and h^(v)(τ_{t_0}) are non-zero in 𝔽_pX_{α_i}; h^(v) comes from H¹(Γ_{F,T∪v}, M_{X_{α_i}}).
items.note: Modifies [FKP19, Proposition 5.9]: Poitou–Tate gives coker Ψ_T ≅ H¹(Γ_{F,T}, ρ̄(𝔤^der)^*)^∨; induction via the Greenberg–Wiles formula and Čebotarev in L K_{ψ_i}∏K_{ω_{i,k}}(μ_{p^c})/F, with only limited freedom in q_i when K_{ψ_i} = K(μ_{p^{D+1}}).

items.name: Proposition 3.6 (second part): classes ramified along a given Z
items.statement: For c ≥ D + 1, L/F as above and non-zero Z ∈ 𝔤^der, there is q_Z ∈ ker((ℤ/p^c)^× → (ℤ/p^D)^×) non-trivial mod p^{D+1} and, for any g_{L/K,Z} ∈ Gal(L/K), a Čebotarev set C_Z of trivial primes (with decomposition groups) containing a positive upper-density l_Z and classes h^(v) ∈ H¹(Γ_{F,T∪v}, ρ̄(𝔤^der)), v ∈ l_Z, with N(v) ≡ q_Z (mod p^c), σ_v ↦ g_{L/K,Z}, h^(v)|_T independent of v, h^(v)(τ_v) and h^(v)(τ_{t_0}) spanning 𝔽_pZ, and h^(v) coming from H¹(Γ_{F,T∪v}, M_Z).
items.note: The analogue of [FKP19, Lemma 5.11], rephrased without semisimplicity of ρ̄(𝔤^der) using the primes t_b and Lemma 3.4(3).

items.name: The cocycles θ_b, θ^(v)_b and η^(v)_b
items.statement: By Lemma 3.4, θ_b ∈ H¹(Γ_{F,T∖(t_0∪{t_{b′}}_{b′≠b})}, 𝔽_p[Γ_F]·e^*_b) with θ_b(τ_{t_b}) = e^*_b, and for a trivial prime v ∉ T, θ^(v)_b ∈ H¹(Γ_{F,(T∖(t_0∪{t_{b′}}))∪v}, 𝔽_p[Γ_F]·e^*_b) with θ^(v)_b(τ_v) = e^*_b; set η^(v)_b = θ_b + θ^(v)_b, so η^(v)_b(τ_v) = η^(v)_b(τ_{t_b}) = e^*_b.

items.name: Lemma 3.7: linear disjointness of the fields K_{η^(v)_b}
items.statement: As the trivial prime v and b ∈ B vary, the fixed fields K_{η^(v)_b} are strongly linearly disjoint over K [FKP19, Notation 5.1], and their composite is linearly disjoint from K_∞ over K.
items.note: Proof: the image of η^(v)_b is the cyclic module generated by η^(v)_b(τ_{t_b}) (resp. τ_v), so a non-trivial intersection would ramify at t_b (resp. v); K_∞/K is unramified away from p.

items.name: Initial mod ϖ² lift and the target local lifts
items.statement: Since Ш²_T(Γ_{F,T}, ρ̄(𝔤^der)) = 0 there is a lift ρ_2 : Γ_{F,T} → G(O/ϖ²) with multiplier μ. Fix target local lifts (λ_w)_{w∈T} of multiplier μ as in [FKP19, Construction 5.6] (unramified for w ∈ T∖S, the λ_w(σ_w) generating Ĝ^der(O/ϖ²) after enlarging T); they differ from ρ_2|_w by z_T = (z_w) ∈ ⊕_{w∈T} H¹(Γ_{F_w}, ρ̄(𝔤^der)). Only the k-linear pairings ⟨·,·⟩ : 𝔤^der × (𝔤^der)^* → k and the k-linear local Tate pairings are used, with the trivial-prime calculation of [FKP19, Lemma 3.9].
items.note: FKP19 = Fakhruddin–Khare–Patrikis, Relative deformation theory, relative Selmer groups, and lifting irreducible Galois representations, Duke Math. J. 170 (2021), no. 16, not yet extracted (a prerequisite); the paper 'does not repeat from [FKP19] any of the local theory' (§1.4).

items.name: Proposition 3.8: the doubling argument mod ϖ²
items.statement: There is a finite index set N and, for each n ∈ N, a positive upper-density set l_n of trivial primes such that for any 2|N|-tuple (A_n, A′_n) of elements of Ĝ^der(O/ϖ²) there are trivial primes Q = (v_n, v′_n)_{n∈N} disjoint from T with {v_n, v′_n} ⊂ l_n and a class h ∈ H¹(Γ_{F,T∪Q}, ρ̄(𝔤^der)) with h|_T = z_T and, for each n, a pair (T_n, α_n) such that (1 + ϖh)ρ_2(τ_{v_n}) = (1 + ϖh)ρ_2(τ_{v′_n}) = u_{α_n}(X_n) for an α_n-root vector X_n, (1 + ϖh)ρ_2(σ_{v_n}) = A_n·z_n and (1 + ϖh)ρ_2(σ_{v′_n}) = A′_n·z′_n with z_n, z′_n ∈ Z_{G^0}(O/ϖ²) ∩ Ĝ(O/ϖ²) (determined by μ).
items.note: h = h_old − Σ_n h^(v_n) + 2Σ_n h^(v′_n) (the 'doubling method' of Khare–Larsen–Ramakrishna 2005, used by Hamblen–Ramakrishna), with a limiting argument over Čebotarev sets using Proposition 3.6 and Lemma 3.7; analogue of [FKP19, Proposition 5.12].

items.name: Assumption 4.1 and Remark 4.2
items.statement: In addition to Assumption 3.1: ρ̄(𝔤^der) has no trivial submodule, and there is no surjection of 𝔽_p[Γ_F]-modules ρ̄(𝔤^der) ↠ W onto an 𝔽_p[Γ_F]-subquotient W of ρ̄(𝔤^der)^*. This forces κ̄ ≠ 1 (μ_p ⊄ F; q ≢ 1 mod p for a function field with constants 𝔽_q), and the second condition follows from: no k[Γ_F]-surjection ρ̄(𝔤^der)^σ ↠ V for σ ∈ Aut(k) and V a k[Γ_F]-subquotient of ρ̄(𝔤^der)^*.

items.name: Lemma 4.3: disjointness of K(ρ_{n−1}(𝔤^der))
items.statement: Let ρ̄ satisfy Assumption 4.1 and ρ_{n−1} : Γ_{F,T_{n−1}} → G(O/ϖ^{n−1}) a lift with T_{n−1} ⊃ T and im(ρ_{n−1}) ⊃ Ĝ^der(O/ϖ^{n−1}). Then L = K(ρ_{n−1}(𝔤^der)) is linearly disjoint over K from K_∞ composed with any fields K_ψ, ψ ∈ H¹(Γ_{F,T_{n−1}}, ρ̄(𝔤^der)^*).
items.note: Proof: Gal(L/K) ≅ Ĝ^der(O/ϖ^{n−1}), whose abelian quotients are controlled by Assumption 4.1 and Lemma 2.1.

items.name: Theorem 4.4: mod ϖ^n lifts with controlled ramification
items.statement: Let p ≫_G 0 and ρ̄ satisfy Assumptions 3.1 and 4.1; fix μ and, for v ∈ S, lifts ρ_v : Γ_{F_v} → G(O) of multiplier μ; T as before Proposition 3.6. There are T ⊂ T_2 ⊂ T_3 ⊂ ⋯ and lifts ρ_n : Γ_{F,T_n} → G(O/ϖ^n) of multiplier μ with ρ_{n+1} ≡ ρ_n (mod ϖ^n) such that: (1) at w ∈ T_n∖S ramified in ρ_n there is (T_w, α_w) with ρ_n(σ_w) ∈ T_w(O/ϖ^n), α_w(ρ_n(σ_w)) ≡ N(w) (mod ϖ^n), ρ_n|_{Γ_{F_w}} ∈ Lift^{μ,α_w}_ρ̄(O/ϖ^n), and either (a) for some s ≤ eD, ρ_s(τ_w) is a non-trivial element of U_{α_w}(O/ϖ^s) and ρ_{n′}|_{Γ_{F_w}} is Ĝ(O)-conjugate to the reduction of a fixed lift ρ_w (a formally smooth point of the generic fibre, as in [FKP19, Lemma 3.7]) for all n′ ≥ s, or (b) for s = eD, ρ_s|_{Γ_{F_w}} is trivial mod centre, α_w(ρ_{s+1}(σ_w)) ≡ N(w) ≢ 1 and β(ρ_{s+1}(σ_w)) ≢ 1 (mod ϖ^{s+1}) for all roots β; (2) ρ_n|_{Γ_{F_v}} is strictly equivalent to ρ_v (mod ϖ^n) for v ∈ S; (3) ρ_n(Γ_F) ⊃ Ĝ^der(O/ϖ^n).
items.note: Proof: Proposition 3.6 with L = K(ρ_{n−1}(𝔤^der)), c = max{D + 1, ⌈n/e⌉}, the g_{L/K,i} chosen trivial for n − 1 ≤ eD and in general position mod ϖ^{eD+1} otherwise; doubling as in Proposition 3.8 and [FKP19, Theorem 5.14].

items.name: Assumption 5.1
items.statement: Let p ≫_G 0 and ρ̄ satisfy Assumptions 3.1 and 4.1, with μ geometric if F is a number field. Assume H⁰(Γ_F, ρ̄(𝔤^der)^*) = 0, and that for all v ∈ S there is a lift ρ_v : Γ_{F_v} → G(O) of type μ (after enlarging O), de Rham and Hodge–Tate regular if v | p.

items.name: G-valued potentially semistable lifting rings R^{□,μ,τ,v}
items.statement: For v | p and a de Rham lift ρ_v : Γ_{F_v} → G(O) (semistable over a finite extension by Berger), Fontaine's construction gives an inertial type τ : I_{F_v} → G(E) up to G^0(E)-conjugacy and a p-adic Hodge type v [BG19 §2.6, Definition 2.8.2]; R^{□,μ,τ,v}_{ρ̄|Γ_{F_v}} is the quotient of the lifting ring whose E-points are the lifts of that type [Bal12, Proposition 3.0.12], and [BG19, Theorem 3.3.3] describes its generic fibre.
items.locator: §1.2, p. 6 and §5, Theorem 5.2 and its proof, pp. 23–24
items.note: Kisin's GL_n rings are planned in LocalGaloisDeformationRings R08.3 and L7 (any rank n); the G-valued rings of Balaji and Bellovin–Gee are not. Routed as a source of L7, where the extraction of Boxer–Calegari–Gee already sent the G-valued ordinary components.

items.name: Theorem 5.2 (= Theorem E): geometric lifts of G-valued residual representations
items.statement: Let p ≫_G 0 and ρ̄ : Γ_{F,S} → G(k) satisfy Assumptions 3.1, 4.1 and 5.1; when F is a number field assume F totally real and ρ̄ odd. Fix an integer t and for each v ∈ S an irreducible component containing ρ_v of R^{□,μ}_{ρ̄|Γ_{F_v}}[1/ϖ] (v ∤ p), resp. R^{□,μ,τ,v}_{ρ̄|Γ_{F_v}}[1/ϖ] (v | p). Then there are a finite E′/E (with O′, k′), depending only on {ρ_v}, a finite set S̃ ⊃ S (which may be taken disjoint from a fixed finite S_0 disjoint from S) and a geometric lift ρ : Γ_{F,S̃} → G(O′) of ρ̄ such that ρ has multiplier μ, ρ(Γ_F) ⊃ Ĝ^der(O′), and for all v ∈ S, ρ|_{Γ_{F_v}} is congruent mod ϖ^t to a Ĝ(O′)-conjugate of ρ_v and lies on the specified component. (S̃ may depend on t; O′ does not.)
items.note: Proof: reduce to G^0 adjoint and a single π_0(G)-orbit of simple factors ([FKP19, Claim 6.13]); replace ρ_v by formally smooth points over O′ ([BG19, Thm 3.3.3], [FKP19, Lemma 4.9]); take M ≥ max{M_1, eD} from [FKP19, Cor. B.2]; run Theorem 4.4 to ρ_N; define the relative Selmer groups and finish as in [FKP19, Theorem 6.11] using Lemma 5.3 and Proposition 5.4. FKP19 = Fakhruddin–Khare–Patrikis, Relative deformation theory, relative Selmer groups, and lifting irreducible Galois representations, Duke Math. J. 170 (2021), no. 16, not yet extracted (a prerequisite); the paper 'does not repeat from [FKP19] any of the local theory' (§1.4).

items.name: Inputs from FKP19: local structure at S and at trivial primes
items.statement: [FKP19, Proposition 4.7] (for a formally smooth point of an irreducible component R_v[1/ϖ], Selmer conditions L_{r,v}, 1 ≤ r ≤ M, with the balanced numerics of its part (3), valid mod ϖ^{n_0}); [FKP19, Lemma 4.9]; [FKP19, Lemmas 3.5, 3.7, 3.9] (the rings Lift^{μ,α} at trivial primes, formally smooth Steinberg-type points, the local duality pairing at trivial primes); [FKP19, Construction 5.6].
items.note: FKP19 = Fakhruddin–Khare–Patrikis, Relative deformation theory, relative Selmer groups, and lifting irreducible Galois representations, Duke Math. J. 170 (2021), no. 16, not yet extracted (a prerequisite); the paper 'does not repeat from [FKP19] any of the local theory' (§1.4). The present paper uses these as black boxes; the Part II must plan them from FKP19 first.

items.name: Input from FKP19: Lazard's bound (Corollary B.2)
items.statement: For Γ the preimage in G^ad(O) of (Ad∘ρ̄)(Γ_{F̃}) ⊂ G^ad(k), there is M_1 such that H¹(Γ, 𝔤^der ⊗_O O/ϖ^M) → H¹(Γ, ρ̄(𝔤^der) ⊗_O k) is zero for all M ≥ M_1.
items.locator: §5, proof of Theorem 5.2, p. 24 (citing [FKP19, Corollary B.2])
items.note: FKP19 = Fakhruddin–Khare–Patrikis, Relative deformation theory, relative Selmer groups, and lifting irreducible Galois representations, Duke Math. J. 170 (2021), no. 16, not yet extracted (a prerequisite); the paper 'does not repeat from [FKP19] any of the local theory' (§1.4). Rests on Lazard's cohomology of p-adic Lie groups.

items.name: Relative Selmer and dual Selmer groups; balance
items.statement: With M, N, S′ = T_N as in the proof of Theorem 5.2, the relative Selmer group H¹_{L_M}(Γ_{F,S′}, ρ_M(𝔤^der)) and relative dual Selmer group H¹_{L_M^⊥}(Γ_{F,S′}, ρ_M(𝔤^der)^*) of [FKP19, Definition 6.2], for Selmer conditions L_{r,v} (from [FKP19, Prop. 4.7] at S, unramified classes where ρ_N is unramified, [FKP19, Lemma 3.5] with s = eD at the new ramified primes). Their Selmer and dual Selmer groups are balanced, |H¹_{L_M}| = |H¹_{L_M^⊥}|, by the Greenberg–Wiles formula (also over function fields), and hence so are the relative groups [FKP19, Lemma 6.3].
items.note: FKP19 = Fakhruddin–Khare–Patrikis, Relative deformation theory, relative Selmer groups, and lifting irreducible Galois representations, Duke Math. J. 170 (2021), no. 16, not yet extracted (a prerequisite); the paper 'does not repeat from [FKP19] any of the local theory' (§1.4).

items.name: Lemma 5.3: vanishing on F*_N
items.statement: With F_r = F(ρ̄, ρ_r(𝔤^der)), F*_M = F_M(μ_{p^{M/e}}), F*_N = F_N(μ_{p^{N/e}}): the map H¹(Gal(F*_N/F), ρ_M(𝔤^der)) → H¹(Gal(F*_N/F), ρ̄(𝔤^der)) is zero, and H¹(Gal(F*_N/F), ρ_M(𝔤^der)^*) = 0.
items.note: Generalises [FKP19, Lemma 6.4]; uses Lemma 2.1 and the choice of M.

items.name: Proposition 5.4: primes killing relative Selmer classes
items.statement: Assume 𝔤^der is a single π_0(G)-orbit of simple factors. Let Q ⊂ Q_N be finite ([FKP19, Definition 6.6]) and 0 ≠ φ ∈ H¹_{L_M}(Γ_{F,S′∪Q}, ρ_M(𝔤^der)), 0 ≠ ψ ∈ H¹_{L_M^⊥}(Γ_{F,S′∪Q}, ρ_M(𝔤^der)^*). There is v ∈ Q_N with torus and root (T, α) such that ψ|_{Γ_{F_v}} ∉ L^{α,⊥}_{1,v} and φ|_{Γ_{F_v}} ∉ L^α_{M,v}.
items.note: Generalises [FKP19, Proposition 6.8]: γ_1 with ρ_N(γ_1) generic and κ(γ_1) ≡ 1 mod ϖ^M but not mod ϖ^{M+1}; Čebotarev for γ_2^rγ_1, r ∈ {0, 1, 2}.

items.name: Corollary 5.5: 𝔤^der = 𝔰𝔩_2 needs only p ≥ 3
items.statement: When 𝔤^der = 𝔰𝔩_2 the bound on p in Theorem 5.2 is p ≥ 3.
items.note: Proof: for p ≥ 3 the trace form is perfect and any non-zero (A, B) ∈ 𝔤^der × (𝔤^der)^* can be conjugated by SL_2(𝔽_p) so that A has non-zero diagonal part and B non-zero 𝔤_{−α}-component; the other uses of p ≫_G 0 are replaced by Lemma 7.1.

items.name: Theorem 5.6: finitely ramified lifts without oddness
items.statement: Let ρ̄ satisfy the hypotheses of Theorem 5.2 except that F is any number field (ρ̄ not assumed totally odd) and, for v | p, ρ̄|_{Γ_{F_v}} has a lift ρ_v of multiplier μ that is a formally smooth point of an irreducible component of R^{□,μ}_{ρ̄|Γ_{F_v}}[1/ϖ] of dimension (1 + [F_v : ℚ_p]) dim G^der. Then for some finite S̃ ⊃ S and O′ ⊃ O, ρ̄ has a lift ρ : Γ_{F,S̃} → G(O′) with image containing Ĝ^der(O′) and ρ|_{Γ_{F_v}} ≡ a Ĝ(O′)-conjugate of ρ_v (mod ϖ^t) for v ∈ S.
items.note: As [FKP19, Theorem 6.21].

items.name: Lemma 6.1: conjugating a lift into the Levi
items.statement: Let ρ : Γ → G(O) be continuous (Γ profinite, G connected), P a parabolic with ρ̄(Γ) ⊂ P(k), T ⊂ B ⊂ P a maximal torus and Borel determining a Levi M and P → M. There are a finite totally ramified K′/K with O′ and g ∈ G(K′) such that gρg^{−1} : Γ → G(O′) reduces to the projection of ρ̄ to M(k). If P is minimal with ρ̄(Γ) ⊂ P(k), gρg^{−1} reduces to 'the' semisimplification of ρ̄.
items.note: Conjugation by a cocharacter η(ϖ′) contracting the unipotent radical.

items.name: Lemma 6.2: large Selmer groups from trivial primes
items.statement: Let W ≠ 0 and W′ be finite-dimensional 𝔽_p[Γ_{F,S}]-modules and W_0 ⊂ W a non-zero subspace. For every n there is a finite set T of W′-trivial primes (N(v) ≡ 1 mod p, W′ trivial as Γ_{F_v}-module) with dim H¹_L(Γ_{F,S∪T}, W) > n, where L_v = 0 for v ∈ S and, for v ∈ T, L_v = homomorphisms Γ_{F_v} → W with I_v mapping into W_0.
items.note: Čebotarev and the Greenberg–Wiles formula.

items.name: Lemma 6.3: making ρ̄ indecomposable inside a parabolic
items.statement: Let G be connected reductive, P ⊊ G parabolic, M ⊃ T a Levi, ρ̄ : Γ_{F,S} → G(k) with image in M(k), and A ⊂ P an abelian unipotent subgroup normalised by M that is a product of root subgroups; P′ = A ⋊ M. There are a finite set T of ρ̄-trivial primes and ρ̄′ : Γ_{F,S∪T} → G(k) with image in P′(k) such that im ρ̄′ ⊃ A(k), the projection of ρ̄′ to M(k) is ρ̄, ρ̄′|_{Γ_{F_v}} ≃ ρ̄|_{Γ_{F_v}} for v ∈ S, and for v ∈ T, ρ̄′(Γ_{F_v}) ⊂ A(k) and ρ̄′(I_v) ⊂ u_α(k) for a root subgroup u_α : 𝔾_a → A.
items.note: Uses Lemma 6.2 for A(k) = ⊕ root spaces.

items.name: Lemma 6.4: local lifts at trivial primes for unipotent ρ̄
items.statement: Let G be connected reductive, T a maximal torus, A a commutative unipotent subgroup and u_α : 𝔾_a → A a root subgroup; F_v local with N(v) ≡ 1 (mod p) and ρ̄ : Γ_{F_v} → G(k) with ρ̄(Γ_{F_v}) ⊂ A(k), ρ̄(I_v) ⊂ u_α(k). If p ≠ 2, ρ̄ lifts to ρ : Γ_{F_v} → G(O).
items.note: ρ̄ is tame; take ρ(τ) = u_2 unipotent and ρ(σ) = t·u_1 with t = α^∨(x), x² = N(v).

items.name: Lemma 6.5: killing H⁰(ρ̄(𝔤^der)) by a non-split extension
items.statement: Let G be connected reductive, P a parabolic with Levi M, p ≫_G 0, and ρ̄ : Γ_{F,S} → G(k) with image in M(k), satisfying the local parts of Assumption 5.1, with H⁰(Γ_{F,S}, ρ̄(𝔤^der)) = 𝔷(M) ∩ 𝔤^der. There are a finite set T of ρ̄-trivial primes and ρ̄′ : Γ_{F,S∪T} → G(k) with image in P(k), projection to M(k) isomorphic to ρ̄, satisfying the local hypotheses of Assumption 5.1, and with H⁰(Γ_{F,S∪T}, ρ̄′(𝔤^der)) = 0.
items.note: Lemma A.7 (applied to G^der) gives A; then Lemmas 6.3 and 6.4.

items.name: Corollary 6.6: lifts of residually Levi-valued ρ̄ with Zariski-dense image
items.statement: Let G be connected reductive, P a parabolic with Levi M, ρ̄ : Γ_{F,S} → G(k) with image in M(k). Assume p ≫_G 0, the local parts of Assumption 5.1, H⁰(Γ_{F,S}, ρ̄(𝔤^der)) = 𝔷(M) ∩ 𝔤^der, H⁰(Γ_{F,S}, ρ̄(𝔤^der)^*) = 0, and either μ_p ⊄ F(ρ̄(𝔤^der)) or (P maximal) ρ̄ satisfies condition (2) of Lemma A.14; choose μ as in Assumption 5.1. Then there are E′/E, S̃ ⊃ S (adding trivial primes) and a geometric lift ρ : Γ_{F,S̃} → G(O′) of ρ̄ with multiplier μ and ρ(Γ_F) ∩ G^der(O′) Zariski-dense in G^der.
items.note: Proof: Lemma 6.5 gives ρ̄′; Lemmas A.5/A.14 and the hypotheses give Assumptions 3.1, 4.1, 5.1 for ρ̄′; Theorem 5.2 lifts ρ̄′; Lemma 6.1 returns to ρ̄.

items.name: Remark 6.7: representations valued in a torus
items.statement: If M is a maximal torus and the image of ρ̄ lies in no proper subtorus, the H⁰(ρ̄(𝔤^der)) condition of Corollary 6.6 holds; H⁰(ρ̄(𝔤^der)^*) = 0 if κ̄^{−1} does not occur in 𝔤^der, and Lemma A.18(3) gives Assumption 4.1: so torus-valued ρ̄ have irreducible geometric lifts under simple conditions. Lemma A.11 gives maximal-parabolic examples.

items.name: Example 6.8: GSp_4 with residual image in the Siegel Levi
items.statement: F = ℚ, G = GSp_4, P the Siegel parabolic (Levi quotient GL_2 × 𝔾_m); ρ̄ = (ρ̄_f, δ) with ρ̄_f absolutely irreducible from a newform on Γ_0(N) of weight r ≥ 2 and δ odd. If ρ̄_f is not dihedral (or, in the dihedral case, κ̄^{r−1} has order > 2 and κ̄^r, κ̄^{r−2} have order > 2), properties (a), (b) of Lemma A.11(2) hold; if the κ̄^{a(r−1)+1} have order ≥ 5 for |a| ≤ 2, Lemma A.14(1), (2) hold (Example A.16); u⁺ ≅ Sym²(ρ̄_f) ⊗ δ^{−1} has no invariants except for at most three δ in the dihedral case. Then ρ̄ has a regular geometric lift ρ : Γ_ℚ → GSp_4(O′) with ρ(Γ_ℚ) ∩ Sp_4(O′) Zariski-dense in Sp_4.
items.note: For fixed r > 2 the order conditions hold for all p ≫ 0.

items.name: Lemma 7.1: the reducible GL_2 hypotheses
items.statement: Let p ≥ 3 and ρ̄ : Γ_{F,S} → GL_2(k) (F totally real) with ρ̄ ∼ (χ̄ ∗; 0 1), χ̄(c_v) = −1 for all v | ∞, χ̄ ≠ κ̄^{−1}, and non-trivial extension class ∗. Then Assumptions 3.1, 4.1 and the first item of Assumption 5.1 hold for ρ̄.
items.note: Proof: the only lines in ρ̄(𝔤^der) and ρ̄(𝔤^der)^* ≅ ρ̄(𝔤^der)(1) are k(χ̄) and k(χ̄κ̄); for χ̄ ≠ κ̄, H¹(Gal(K/F), ρ̄(𝔤^der)^*) reduces to Hom_{Gal(K_0/F)}(P, k(ψ)) for ψ ∈ {χ̄^{−1}κ̄, κ̄, χ̄κ̄}, P the p-Sylow subgroup, K_0 = F(χ̄, μ_p), and P ≅ ⊕𝔽_p(χ̄); the case χ̄ = κ̄ is a cocycle computation on the filtration F_2 ⊂ F_1 ⊂ F_0 = ρ̄(𝔤^der)^*. Two misprints on p. 32 (source issues E1, E2).

items.name: Lemma 7.2(1): local lifts away from p with given determinant
items.statement: Let p ≥ 3, ρ̄ ∼ (χ̄ ∗; 0 1) on Γ_{F,S}, and μ : Γ_{F,S} → O^× a geometric lift of det ρ̄ = χ̄ of the form κ^{r−1}χ_0 (r ≥ 2, χ_0 of finite order). After enlarging O, for v ∈ S not above p there is a lift ρ_v : Γ_{F_v} → GL_2(O′) of ρ̄|_{Γ_{F_v}} with determinant μ.
items.note: Proof: [Dia97] and [Tay03, §1, E3] (formally smooth components), with square roots of characters. LocalGaloisDeformationRings R08.2 plans the conditions away from p; the existence of such lifts for reducible ρ̄ with prescribed determinant belongs there.

items.name: Lemma 7.2(2): ordinary potentially crystalline lifts at p
items.statement: In the setting of Lemma 7.2(1), for v | p there is an ordinary potentially crystalline lift ρ_v : Γ_{F_v} → GL_2(O′) of ρ̄|_{Γ_{F_v}} with Hodge–Tate weights {0, r − 1} and determinant μ; and there is always an ordinary potentially crystalline lift with Hodge–Tate weights {0, r − 1} having a non-trivial unramified quotient, possibly without det ρ_v = μ. (ρ̄|_{Γ_{F_v}} is called ordinary when it is F′_v-ordinary in the sense of Definition B.2.)
items.note: Proof: [BLGG12, Lemma 6.1.6] extended to general r, distinguishing peu and très ramifiée extensions. Routed as a source of LocalGaloisDeformationRings R08.6 (local statements for the global arguments).

items.name: Lemma 7.2(3): a crystalline lift in Serre's weight
items.statement: When F = ℚ (or F is split at all places above p) and r = k(ρ̄|_{Γ_{ℚ_p}}) is Serre's weight [Ser87, §2.3], there is a crystalline lift ρ_p : Γ_{ℚ_p} → GL_2(O′) of ρ̄|_{Γ_{ℚ_p}} with Hodge–Tate weights {0, r − 1}.
items.note: Proof: [BDJ10, §3.2]. Routed as a source of R08.6.

items.name: Serre's weight k(ρ̄|_{Γ_{ℚ_p}})
items.statement: The weight attached to ρ̄|_{Γ_{ℚ_p}} by Serre's recipe [Ser87, §2.3], including the reducible local cases.
items.note: AlgebraicModularFormsAndSerreWeights R15.4 plans Serre's full piecewise recipe, including reducible local representations.

items.name: Lemma 7.3: the semisimplification of an odd ρ̄ is modular
items.statement: Let ρ̄ : Γ_{ℚ,S} → GL_2(k) be continuous and odd. Then ρ̄^{ss} is isomorphic to the semisimplification of a residual representation arising from ρ_{f,ι} for a newform f ∈ S_r(Γ_1(N)), some N ≥ 1, r ≥ 2.
items.note: Irreducible case: Serre's conjecture (Khare–Wintenberger), planned in ClassicalSerreModularity R27.6. Reducible case (folklore, [SW99, §3.4]): an Eisenstein series E_r ∈ M_r(Γ_1(N)) (N divisible by a prime q ≡ 1 mod p) whose constant terms vanish mod ℘ is congruent to a newform; or use the reduction of an Eisenstein series and Θ^{p−1}-type arguments. Not planned; routed to the Part II's modularity layer.

items.name: Skinner–Wiles: modularity of residually reducible ordinary representations
items.statement: [SW99, main theorem]: an odd irreducible p-adic ρ : Γ_ℚ → GL_2(O), unramified outside finitely many primes, ordinary at p with residual semisimplification 1 ⊕ χ̄ and χ̄|_{Γ_{ℚ_p}} ≠ 1 (with the paper's further hypotheses), arises from a newform. [SW99, Theorems A, B] give analogues over certain totally real fields (Remark 7.5).
items.locator: §7, proof of Theorem 7.4 and Remark 7.5, pp. 35–36 (cited)
items.note: OrdinaryAutomorphicFormsAndModularityLifting R21.5 plans the Skinner–Wiles residually reducible ordinary results.

items.name: Pan: the residually reducible Fontaine–Mazur theorem (ordinary case with χ̄|_{Γ_{ℚ_p}} = 1)
items.statement: [Pan19]: for p odd, an odd irreducible ρ : Γ_ℚ → GL_2(E), finitely ramified, de Rham at p with distinct Hodge–Tate weights, whose residual semisimplification is a sum of two characters χ̄_1 ⊕ χ̄_2 (with χ̄_1/χ̄_2|_{Γ_{ℚ_p}} ≠ ω when p = 3), arises from a cuspidal eigenform up to twist; the paper uses the ordinary case χ̄|_{Γ_{ℚ_p}} = 1 left open by Skinner–Wiles (Pan's §6), where the lift may be non-distinguished at p.
items.locator: §7, proof of Theorem 7.4, p. 35 (cited); Pan, arXiv 1901.07166v2, Theorem 1.0.2
items.note: GL2ModularityLifting R32.4 plans Pan's residually reducible theorem (for p ≥ 5 as needed there) and R21.5 the ordinary p = 3 branch; the ordinary theorem for all odd p (Pan §6, Theorem 6.1.2) should be recorded there. Pan's Theorem 1.0.2 was read to confirm the p = 3 condition does not bite: χ̄|_{Γ_{ℚ_3}} = 1 ≠ ω.

items.name: Serre's conjecture (Khare–Wintenberger)
items.statement: An odd, irreducible, continuous ρ̄ : Gal(ℚ̄/ℚ) → GL_2(k) arises from a newform (of Serre's weight and level).
items.note: ClassicalSerreModularity R27.6 plans the full classical statement.

items.name: Theorem 7.4 (= Theorem B): modularity of reducible odd ρ̄ : Γ_ℚ → GL_2(k)
items.statement: Let p ≥ 3 and ρ̄ : Γ_{ℚ,S} → GL_2(k) continuous with ρ̄ ∼ (χ̄ ∗; 0 1), χ̄(c) = −1 and χ̄ ≠ κ̄^{−1}. Then ρ̄ is modular; more precisely, for any r ≥ 2, ρ̄ is modular of weight r and some level; and ρ̄ is modular of weight k(ρ̄|_{Γ_{ℚ_p}}) and level prime to p.
items.note: Proof (∗ ≠ 0): Lemmas 7.1, 7.2 and Corollary 5.5 give Theorem 5.2 for G = GL_2 with determinant μ = κ^{r−1}χ_0 (Kronecker–Weber for χ_0, planned in Tau Ceti's ClassFieldTheory Layer 13) and ordinary components (Lemma B.4); the lift is modular by Skinner–Wiles (χ̄|_{Γ_{ℚ_p}} ≠ 1) or Pan (χ̄|_{Γ_{ℚ_p}} = 1), the weight by local–global compatibility at p (AutomorphicGaloisRepresentations R19.5). Split case: Lemma 6.3 then Theorem 5.2 and Lemma 6.1, or Lemma 7.3 and Lemma 6.1. Improves Theorem A by dropping its conditions (2), (3) and all but one exceptional χ̄. The condition χ̄ ≠ κ̄^{−1} is expected to be superfluous (Conjecture D).

items.name: Remark 7.5: totally real fields and the role of lifting
items.statement: Since [SW99, Theorems A, B] include residually reducible modularity over certain totally real fields, the method gives mod p modularity there too; lifting reducible ρ̄ to irreducible geometric ρ (introduced in [HR08]) is at present the only route to modularity of residually reducible representations, as it was for Serre's conjecture [KW09b, KW09c].

items.name: Lemma 7.6: infinitely many extensions with the same semisimplification
items.statement: Let Γ be a finite group, L an infinite field and φ : Γ → L^×. If dim_L H¹(Γ, L(φ)) > 1 or dim_L H¹(Γ, L(φ^{−1})) > 1, there are infinitely many pairwise non-conjugate (under GL_2(L)) ρ : Γ → GL_2(L) with semisimplification id ⊕ φ.
items.note: Implicit in Berger–Klosin [BK19]. Proof: the isomorphism classes are {0} ∪ ℙ^{n−1}(L) ∪ ℙ^{m−1}(L), n = dim H¹(Γ, L(φ)), m = dim H¹(Γ, L(φ^{−1})) (the two projective spaces identified if φ = 1).

items.name: Serre's lemma: stable lattices and the Bruhat–Tits tree
items.statement: For an irreducible ρ : Γ_ℚ → GL_2(E) whose residual semisimplification is 1 ⊕ χ̄ with 1 ≠ χ̄, the fixed points of ρ(Γ_ℚ) in the Bruhat–Tits tree of PGL_2(E) form a segment. If it is an edge, exactly two residual representations arise from stable lattices (the end points: non-split extensions of 1 by χ̄ and of χ̄ by 1); if it has length > 1, the split representation also arises (interior vertices). The set X_E of indecomposable reductions up to GL_2(k′)-conjugacy is in bijection with X_{E′} for finite E′/E.
items.note: [BC14, Propositions 11, 32], [Bel, §1]. ReductiveGroupsPartII RG2.2 plans buildings and the SL_2 tree as an example, but not this Galois statement. Routed to the Part II with Proposition 7.7.

items.name: Proposition 7.7: only finitely many reducible ρ̄ at fixed weight and level
items.statement: Let Γ be a finite quotient of Γ_ℚ and χ̄ : Γ → k^× a non-trivial odd character with dim_k H¹(Γ, k(χ̄)) > 1. For fixed N ≥ 1 and r ≥ 2, only finitely many of the infinitely many non-isomorphic ρ : Γ → GL_2(k̄) with semisimplification id ⊕ χ̄ (Lemma 7.6) arise from reductions of Galois-stable lattices in ρ_{f,ι} for newforms f ∈ S_r(Γ_1(N)).
items.note: Proof: Serre's lemma and finiteness of dim S_r(Γ_1(N)). So minimal lifts, which the Khare–Wintenberger method produces, need not exist.

items.name: Remark 7.8: why the Khare–Wintenberger lifting method fails
items.statement: For any χ̄ : Γ_ℚ → k^×, Lemma 6.2 gives a finite quotient Γ of Γ_{ℚ,S} through which χ̄ factors with dim_k H¹(Γ, k(χ̄)) > 1. The method of [KW09a] bounds deformation rings above (R/pR finite, via some version of [dJ01, Lemma 3.15], which may fail for residually reducible ρ̄) and below (dim R > 0) and produces minimal lifts, which by Proposition 7.7 may not exist in the residually reducible case.

items.name: L. Lafforgue: Galois representations of cuspidal π of GL_n over function fields
items.statement: For a global function field F of characteristic ℓ ≠ p, ι : ℂ ≅ ℚ̄_p and π cuspidal automorphic on GL_n(𝔸_F) with central character of finite order, there is ρ_{π,ι} : Γ_F → GL_n(ℚ̄_p) attached to π [Laf02, Théorème, p. 2; Théorème VI.1.1], and conversely every irreducible ℓ-adic representation with finite-order determinant arises (the correspondence).
items.note: GlobalShtukasAndFunctionFieldLanglands GS.6 plans L. Lafforgue's GL_n correspondence.

items.name: Automorphic ρ̄ over a function field
items.statement: ρ̄ : Γ_F → GL_n(k) is automorphic if, after extension of scalars, it is isomorphic to the reduction ρ̄_{π,ι} : Γ_F → GL_n(O_E/m_E) of some ρ_{π,ι}-stable lattice, for π cuspidal with central character of finite order.
items.note: The lattice-sensitive notion again (not only the semisimplification).

items.name: Local lifts in equal characteristic (after Clozel–Harris–Taylor)
items.statement: For F a global function field of characteristic ℓ ≠ p and v a place, every ρ̄ : Γ_{F_v} → GL_n(k) has a p-adic lift, as in [CHT08, Corollary 2.4.21]: §2.4.4 of loc. cit. uses only that the kernel of any surjection I_{F_v} → ℤ_p has pro-order prime to p and the structure of the maximal tame extension with p-power ramification index. Since p ∤ n, any character Γ_{F_v} → 1 + ϖO has an n-th root, so the multiplier can be matched to a global μ.
items.note: LocalGaloisDeformationRings R08.2 plans minimally ramified conditions at places of number fields; the equal-characteristic existence statement is not planned. Routed as a source of R08.2.

items.name: Theorem 8.1: automorphy of reducible ρ̄ over function fields
items.statement: Let p ≫_n 0, F a global function field of characteristic ≠ p, and ρ̄ : Γ_{F,S} → GL_n(k) continuous satisfying Assumptions 3.1, 4.1 and the first part of Assumption 5.1. Then ρ̄ is automorphic.
items.note: Proof: the second part of Assumption 5.1 holds automatically (local lifts above), then Theorem 5.2 gives a finitely ramified lift and L. Lafforgue (GS.6) makes it automorphic.

items.name: Remark 8.2: the absolutely irreducible case was known
items.statement: When ρ̄ is absolutely irreducible the hypotheses of Theorem 8.1 hold for p ≫_n 0; this case is already known: for p ∤ n de Jong's conjecture [dJ01, Conj. 2.3] implies by [dJ01, Thm 3.5] (and [BHKT19, Thm 5.13] when ρ̄|_{Γ_{F𝔽̄}} is reducible) that ρ̄ has a lift unramified outside S; Gaitsgory [Gai07] proved de Jong's conjecture modulo results widely held to be straightforward adaptations (étale k[[t]]-sheaves, a complete proof of [MV07, Thm 14.1] with general coefficients).
items.note: BHKT19 Theorem 5.13 is routed by that paper's extraction to its proposed Part II GValuedDeformationsAndPotentialAutomorphy; de Jong's conjecture is not in the atlas. Recorded in the Part II's function-field application with those dependencies stated.

items.name: Corollary 8.3 (= Theorem C): maximal parabolic case over function fields
items.statement: Let p ≫_n 0, F a global function field of characteristic ℓ ≠ p, and ρ̄ : Γ_{F,S} → GL_n(k) factoring through a maximal parabolic P with Levi quotient M ≅ GL_{n_1} × GL_{n_2}; ρ̄_M = ρ̄_1 ⊕ ρ̄_2, ordered so that ρ̄ is an extension of ρ̄_2 by ρ̄_1. Assume ρ̄_M absolutely irreducible (as an M-valued representation), ρ̄_1 ≄ ρ̄_2 ⊗ ψ̄ for ψ̄ ∈ {1, κ̄^{−1}} (automatic if n_1 ≠ n_2), and, for χ̄ = det(ρ̄_1)^{n_2/d}·det(ρ̄_2)^{−n_1/d}, d = gcd(n_1, n_2), [F(ζ_p) : F(ζ_p) ∩ F(χ̄)] > b(n_1, n_2). Then ρ̄ is automorphic.
items.note: Proof: Lemma A.14(1) gives μ_p ⊄ F(ρ̄(𝔤^der)) and Assumption 3.1 and the second part of 4.1; non-split case by Lemma A.11(1) and Theorem 8.1; split case by Lemma 6.5, Lemma A.11(1), Theorem 8.1 and Lemma 6.1. The κ̄-twisted case ρ̄_1 ≅ ρ̄_2 ⊗ κ̄ is not excluded but made vacuous by the third hypothesis (p. 39).

items.name: Corollary 8.4: direct sums over function fields
items.statement: Let p ≫_n 0 and ρ̄ = ⊕_{i=1}^r ρ̄_i : Γ_{F,S} → GL_n(k), r > 1, with (1) each ρ̄_i absolutely irreducible, (2) ρ̄_i ≄ ρ̄_j ⊗ ψ̄ for ψ̄ ∈ {1, κ̄, κ̄^{−1}}, i ≠ j, (3) [F(ζ_p) : F(ζ_p) ∩ F(χ̄_{i,j})] > b(n) for χ̄_{i,j} = det(ρ̄_i)^{n_j}·det(ρ̄_j)^{−n_i}, i ≠ j. Then ρ̄ is automorphic.
items.note: Proof: Lemma A.9, Corollary 6.6 (with Theorem 8.1's remarks) and Lafforgue.

items.name: ι-ordinary automorphic representations and ξ-ordinary Galois representations
items.statement: π is ι-ordinary if it satisfies [Tho15, Lemma 2.3]; for K/ℚ_p finite and ξ = (ξ_τ)_τ, ξ_τ ∈ ℤ^n_+ (ξ_1 ≥ ⋯ ≥ ξ_n), ρ : Γ_K → GL_n(ℚ̄_p) is ξ-ordinary if it satisfies [Tho15, Definition 2.5]: ρ is an iterated extension of characters ψ_1, …, ψ_n (upper triangular) with τ-labelled Hodge–Tate weight of ψ_i equal to −(ξ_{τ,n−i+1} + i − 1), strictly increasing in i. Such ρ are de Rham ([Nek93, Proposition 1.28]).
items.note: The extraction of Boxer–Calegari–Gee routed 'ι-ordinary and ordinarily automorphic' to the proposed Part II PolarizedAutomorphyLifting; this item joins it.

items.name: Allen–Newton–Thorne: automorphy lifting for residually reducible representations
items.statement: [ANT20, Theorem 1.1]: over a CM field L′, an ι-ordinary (essentially conjugate self-dual) ρ : Γ_{L′} → GL_{2n}(ℚ̄_p) satisfying hypotheses (1)–(8) of loc. cit. — including that L′(ζ_p) ⊄ L′(ρ̄(𝔤^der)), that the ρ̄_i|_{Γ_{L′(ζ_p)}} are absolutely irreducible and distinct, that ρ̄ = ρ̄^{ss} has no quotient of order p, that ρ̄ is not induced, residual automorphy by an ι-ordinary π, and p large — is automorphic: ρ ≅ r_ι(Π) for a RACSDC Π of GL_{2n}(𝔸_{L′}).
items.note: The extraction of Newton–Thorne 2021 routed the Allen–Newton–Thorne theorems to the proposed Part II PolarizedAutomorphyLifting; joins it.

items.name: Barnet-Lamb–Gee–Geraghty–Taylor: residual potential automorphy with a Steinberg place
items.statement: [BLGGT14, Theorem 3.1.2] applied to ρ̄ : Γ_F → GSp_{2n}(k) (the set I a singleton; ρ̄ may be reducible) with F_avoid = F(ρ̄, ζ_p): there is a Galois totally real F′/F linearly disjoint from F(ρ̄, ζ_p) and a regular algebraic self-dual cuspidal π of GL_{2n}(𝔸_{F′}) with ρ̄|_{Γ_{F′}} ≃ r̄_ι(π), π ι-ordinary of weight 0, and — adding to the Moret-Bailly argument ([BLGGT14, Prop. 3.1.1], on T_{ρ̄ × ρ̄′} over F(ζ_N)^+) the local condition v(t(P)) < 0 above v_0 — π_{v_0} an unramified twist of Steinberg ([BLGHT11, Lemma 5.1(2)] and local–global compatibility).
items.note: ModularityAndLanglandsExtensions ML.2 is the atlas's potential automorphy assembly, and PotentialModularityAndCompatibleSystems R23.1 plans Moret-Bailly; the Steinberg-at-v_0 modification is the paper's. Routed as a source of ML.2.

items.name: Compatible systems from potential automorphy (BLGGT14, Theorem 5.5.1)
items.statement: The argument of [BLGGT14, Theorem 5.5.1]: a ρ that is automorphic over a suitable F′ (ρ|_{Γ_{F′}} ≅ r_ι(Π_{F′}), Π_{F′} RAESDC) belongs to a strictly pure compatible system {ρ_{ι′}} of ℓ-adic representations of Γ_F indexed by ι′ : ℂ ≅ ℚ̄_ℓ; descent from L′ = LF′ to F′ uses Gal(L′/F′)-invariance and a twist by δ_{L′/F′}.
items.note: Routed with the previous item as a source of ModularityAndLanglandsExtensions ML.2 ('track compatible systems and descent'); PotentialAutomorphyInfrastructure PA.5 supplies the compatible-system operations.

items.name: Local lifts for GSp_2n: Booher's minimally ramified lifts and Steinberg points
items.statement: For v ∤ p, ρ̄|_{Γ_{F_v}} has a lift Γ_{F_v} → GSp_{2n}(O′) with multiplier κ^{1−2n} lying on an irreducible component of R^{□,κ^{1−2n}}_{ρ̄|Γ_{F_v}} isomorphic to O′[[X_1, …, X_{dim G^der}]] ([Boo19]); at a trivial prime v_0, a lift whose Weil–Deligne representation is a twist of the Steinberg parameter is a formally smooth point of R^{□,κ^{1−2n}}_{ρ̄|Γ_{F_{v_0}}} (via [BG19]; cf. [FKP19, Lemma 3.7]).
items.note: G-valued local deformation theory away from p is not planned (R08.2 is GL_2). Routed as a source of LocalGaloisDeformationRings R08.2.

items.name: Dynkin: Zariski closures containing a regular unipotent
items.statement: A Zariski-closed subgroup of GSp_{2n} containing a regular unipotent element of GL_{2n}, acting symplectically, has identity component a principal GL_2 or all of GSp_{2n} (SO_{2n} contains no regular unipotent of GL_{2n}); independence of ℓ of the formal character (the rank of a maximal torus) excludes the principal GL_2 for n > 1.
items.note: Dynkin's classification of subgroups containing a regular unipotent. Not in the atlas.

items.name: Proposition 9.1: GSp_2n compatible systems lifting reducible ρ̄
items.statement: Let F be totally real, n ≥ 1, p ≫_n 0 with [F(ζ_p) : F] > a_{GSp_{2n}} ([FKP19, Lemma A.6]), and ρ̄ : Γ_{F,S} → GSp_{2n}(k) with absolutely GSp_{2n}-irreducible restriction to Γ_{F(ζ_p)} and similitude κ̄^{1−2n}. Assume for all v | p a lift ρ_v : Γ_{F_v} → GSp_{2n}(O) with similitude κ^{1−2n} that is ordinary of some weight ξ_v in GL_{2n}, and that ρ̄ (in GL_{2n}) is not induced from a proper subgroup. Then there are S̃ ⊃ S, O′ ⊃ O and a geometric lift ρ : Γ_{F,S̃} → GSp_{2n}(O′) with Zariski-dense image belonging to a strictly pure compatible system ρ_ι : Γ_F → GSp_{2n}(ℚ̄_ℓ), each with Zariski-dense image.
items.note: Proof: [FKP19, Theorem A] (or Theorem E) with ordinary components (Lemma B.4) and a Steinberg place v_0; BLGGT14 residual potential automorphy; ANT20 over L′ = LF′; descent; BLGGT14 Theorem 5.5.1; Dynkin. Remark: [NT19, Cor. 5.2] gives essentially conjugate self-dual lifts over a CM extension, and [FKP20] discusses the Khare–Wintenberger method in GL-reducible settings.

items.name: Properties (C1)–(C4) and the parabolic set-up
items.statement: (C1) ρ̄(𝔤^der) has no trivial submodule; (C2) ρ̄(𝔤^der)^* has no trivial submodule; (C3) there is no surjection of 𝔽_p[Γ_F]-modules ρ̄(𝔤^der) ↠ W with W ≠ 0 a subquotient of ρ̄(𝔤^der)^*; (C4) H¹(Gal(K/F), ρ̄(𝔤^der)^*) = 0. ρ̄ factors through P(k), P a proper parabolic of a split connected reductive G, minimal with this property; π : P → M the Levi quotient, ρ̄_M = π∘ρ̄, U the unipotent radical, 𝔲 = Lie U, U^−, 𝔲^−; {𝔲_i}, {U_i} the ascending central series.
items.note: (C1)–(C4) imply Assumptions 3.1, 4.1 and the first part of 5.1.

items.name: Lemma A.1: a P-equivariant exponential
items.statement: If p ≫_G 0 there is a P-equivariant isomorphism of varieties exp : 𝔲 → U over k restricting to exp : 𝔲_i → U_i and inducing P-equivariant isomorphisms of algebraic groups 𝔲_{i+1}/𝔲_i → U_{i+1}/U_i; log = exp^{−1}. (Remark A.2: for GL_n, p > n suffices.)
items.locator: Appendix A, Lemma A.1 and Remark A.2, p. 44
items.note: Characteristic zero, then spreading out from the split model over ℤ.

items.name: Lemma A.3: Jordan–Hölder for central Γ-chains of a p-group
items.statement: Let Γ act on a finite p-group Σ. For maximal chains {1} = Σ_0 ⊊ ⋯ ⊊ Σ_n = Σ of normal Γ-invariant subgroups with Σ_{i+1}/Σ_i central in Σ/Σ_i (so each factor is a simple 𝔽_p[Γ]-module), the multiset of factors is independent of the chain.
items.note: [Isa09, Theorem 10.5]. Mathlib has the abstract theorem (JordanHolderLattice, CompositionSeries.jordan_holder in Mathlib/Order/JordanHolder.lean) but not this operator-group instance. One index misprint (source issue E3).

items.name: Lemma A.4: factors of the image of Γ in U are subquotients of 𝔲
items.statement: Suppose p ≫_G 0. Let Γ ⊂ P(k), Γ̄ its image in M(k) and Σ = ker(Γ → Γ̄) ⊂ U(k), with ascending central series {Σ_i}. Every irreducible Γ̄-subquotient of Σ_{i+1}/Σ_i is isomorphic to an 𝔽_p[Γ̄]-subquotient of 𝔲.
items.note: Lemmas A.1 and A.3.

items.name: Lemma A.5: μ_p ⊄ F(ρ̄(𝔤^der)) gives (C3) and (C4)
items.statement: If p ≫_G 0 and μ_p ⊄ F(ρ̄(𝔤^der)), then (C3) and (C4) hold (even for the semisimplification of ρ̄(𝔤^der)). Whether μ_p ⊂ F(ρ̄(𝔤^der)) depends only on ρ̄_M (Remark A.6).
items.locator: Appendix A, Lemma A.5 and Remark A.6, p. 45
items.note: Proof: V″ and V″ ⊗ κ̄ would both be subquotients; for (C4), [Gur99, Theorem A] (as in [FKP19, Lemma A.1]) over F′ = F(ρ̄_M, κ̄), inflation–restriction and Lemma A.4.

items.name: Guralnick: small representations are completely reducible
items.statement: [Gur99, Theorem A] (small representations are completely reducible), as the paper uses it: for p ≫_G 0 and ρ̄_M absolutely irreducible, the k[Γ_F]-modules built from ρ̄_M on 𝔪′, 𝔲, 𝔲^− and ρ̄(𝔤^der)^{ss} are semisimple; with [FKP19, Lemmas A.1, A.2, A.6, Corollary A.6] this gives H¹(Gal(F′/F), W) = 0 for absolutely irreducible subquotients W of ρ̄(𝔤^der)^*, semisimplicity of 𝔪′, 𝔲, 𝔲^− as ρ̄_M-modules, Z(𝔪′) = H⁰(Γ_F, ρ̄(𝔪′)) for maximal P, and the bound a_G on cyclic quotients of the image modulo the centre.
items.note: Group-theoretic inputs of the criteria; not in the atlas. FKP19 = Fakhruddin–Khare–Patrikis, Relative deformation theory, relative Selmer groups, and lifting irreducible Galois representations, Duke Math. J. 170 (2021), no. 16, not yet extracted (a prerequisite); the paper 'does not repeat from [FKP19] any of the local theory' (§1.4).

items.name: Lemma A.7: an abelian root subgroup on which the centre of M acts faithfully
items.statement: Let G be semisimple, P a parabolic with unipotent radical U and Levi M, p ≫_G 0. There is a subgroup A ⊂ U that is a product of root subgroups, normalised by M, with 𝔷(M) = Lie Z(M) acting faithfully on 𝔞 = Lie A.
items.note: Proof: a maximal abelian M-submodule 𝔞 ⊂ 𝔲 has this property (otherwise enlarge it by 𝔞′ ⊂ 𝔲_f with 2f ∉ R). Remark A.8: for L-faithful maximal parabolics (all maximal parabolics in type A; one exists for every simple G by [Sha10, App. A]) one may take A = Z(U).

items.name: Lemma A.9: criteria for GL_n
items.statement: Let P ⊂ GL_n be the standard parabolic for n = n_1 + ⋯ + n_r (r > 1), M = ∏GL_{n_i}, and ρ̄ with image in P(k) and projections ρ̄_i. If p ≫_n 0 and (1) each ρ̄_i is absolutely irreducible, (2) ρ̄_i ≄ ρ̄_j ⊗ ψ̄ for ψ̄ ∈ {1, κ̄, κ̄^{−1}}, i ≠ j, (3) [F(ζ_p) : F(ζ_p) ∩ F(χ̄_{i,j})] > b(n) for χ̄_{i,j} = det(ρ̄_i)^{n_j} det(ρ̄_j)^{−n_i}, then H⁰(Γ_F, ρ̄(𝔤^der)) ⊂ 𝔷(M) ∩ 𝔤^der and (C2), (C3), (C4) hold.
items.note: Uses [FKP19, Lemma A.6] and Lemma A.5.

items.name: Lemma A.10: criteria for the group G_n of Clozel–Harris–Taylor
items.statement: Let G = G_n [CHT08, §2.1] (G^0 ≅ GL_n × 𝔾_m, G/G^0 ≅ ℤ/2), ρ̄ : Γ_F → G(k) with L/F (cut out by G/G^0) a CM extension, r̄ = ⊕_{i=1}^s r̄_i the GL_n-part of ρ̄|_{Γ_L}, p ≫_n 0. If (1) each r̄_i is absolutely irreducible, (2) r̄_i ≄ r̄_j ⊗ ψ̄ for ψ̄ ∈ {1, κ̄, κ̄^{−1}}, i ≠ j, (3) [F(ζ_p) : F(ζ_p) ∩ F(χ̄_{i,j})] > b(n) for χ̄_{i,j} = det(r̄_i)^{n_j} det(r̄_j)^{−n_i}, then (C1)–(C4) hold.
items.note: Complex conjugation acts on 𝔤_n by x ↦ −ᵗx, giving (C1) for p ≠ 2. Index misprint in (1) (source issue E4).

items.name: Lemma A.11: maximal parabolics with abelian unipotent radical
items.statement: Suppose [F(ζ_p) : F] ≫_G 0, P maximal and ρ̄_M absolutely irreducible, with (G, P) one of: (1) GL_n, P for n = n′ + n″ (ρ̄ an extension of ρ̄″_M by ρ̄′_M); (a) n odd, or n′ = n″ and ρ̄′_M ≄ ρ̄″_M; (b) n odd, or n′ = n″ and ρ̄′_M ≄ ρ̄″_M ⊗ κ̄^{−1}; (2) GSp_{2n}, Siegel parabolic, M ≅ GL_n × 𝔾_m: (a) ρ̄′_M preserves no non-degenerate symmetric form, (b) none up to scalar with multiplier κ̄; (3) SO_n, stabiliser of an isotropic line, M ≅ SO_{n−2} × 𝔾_m: (a) ρ̄′_M has no invariant vector, (b) no κ̄^{±1}-invariant vector; (4) SO_{2n}, stabiliser of a maximal isotropic subspace, M ≅ GL_n: (a) ρ̄_M preserves no non-degenerate alternating form, (b) none up to scalar with multiplier κ̄. If ρ̄(Γ_F) → M(k) is not injective, (a) implies (C1) and (b) implies (C2).
items.note: Proof: (𝔤^der)^{ss} = 𝔪′ ⊕ 𝔲 ⊕ 𝔲^− semisimple by [Gur99]; the M-action on 𝔲 is λ_1 ⊗ λ_2^∨, Sym², std ⊠ std, ∧² in cases (1)–(4); centralisers of semisimple elements are connected reductive [Ste75, Theorem 3.14]. Remark A.12: similar conditions for any maximal P from [Sha10, Apps. A, B].

items.name: Definition A.13: property D(s, t, N)
items.statement: For P maximal, let χ : Γ_F → 𝔾_m(k) be the composite Γ_F → P(k) → M̄(k) → 𝔾_m(k) (M̄ the Levi quotient of the image of P in G^ad). ρ̄ satisfies D(s, t, N) if for all σ ∈ Aut(k), all F′/F with [F′ : F] ≤ N and all m_1, m_2 ∈ ℤ with |m_1|, |m_2| ≤ t, (χ^{m_1})^σ|_{Γ_{F′}} ≠ (χ^{m_2} ⊗ κ̄^s)|_{Γ_{F′}}.
items.note: Γ′_F printed for Γ_{F′} (source issue E5).

items.name: Lemma A.14: (C3) and (C4) for maximal parabolics
items.statement: Suppose p ≫_G 0, P maximal and ρ̄_M absolutely irreducible. There are b, s, t, N depending only on the root datum of (G, P) such that if (1) [F(κ̄) : F(κ̄) ∩ F(χ)] > b, or (2) ρ̄ satisfies D(s, t, N), then (C3) and (C4) hold; in case (1), μ_p ⊄ F(ρ̄(𝔤^der)).
items.note: Proof: case (1) via Remark A.6, [FKP19, Lemma A.6] and Lemma A.5; case (2) via the characters χ_1, …, χ_r of Z(M) on 𝔲, [FKP19, Cor. A.6] and inflation–restriction. Remark A.15: if χ is 𝔽_p^×-valued, σ may be ignored and (2) holds for χ = κ̄^n except for at most n_G classes mod p − 1.

items.name: Examples A.16 and A.17: GSp_4 Siegel and GL_{2n} with blocks n + n
items.statement: GSp_4, Siegel P (M = GL_2 × 𝔾_m, M̄^ad = PGL_2): N = 4, and N = 2 except in the A_4 case (N = 3) and the even dihedral case, s = 1, χ = det∘ρ̄_1 for ρ̄_M = (ρ̄_1, δ); if χ is 𝔽_p^×-valued, (C3), (C4) hold when χ^a ⊗ κ̄ has order ≥ 5 for |a| ≤ 2. GL_{2n}, P for 2n = n + n: one character of Z(M(k)) on 𝔲, s = n, N the largest abelianisation of an absolutely irreducible subgroup of PGL_n(k) × PGL_n(k); (C3), (C4) hold if (χ^{±1})^σ|_{Γ_{F′}} ≠ (χ^{±1} ⊗ κ̄^n)|_{Γ_{F′}} for [F′ : F] ≤ N.
items.locator: Appendix A.2, Examples A.16, A.17, p. 50
items.note: Dickson's classification of finite subgroups of PGL_2(k).

items.name: Lemma A.18: criteria for Borel-valued ρ̄
items.statement: Let ρ̄ : Γ_F → G(k) with im ρ̄ ⊂ B(k), p ≫_G 0; U(ρ̄) = U(k) ∩ im ρ̄, 𝔲(ρ̄) the span of log U(ρ̄), Z(𝔲(ρ̄)) its centraliser in 𝔤^der. (1) If the trivial character does not occur in Z(𝔲(ρ̄))^{ss}, (C1) holds; (2) if κ̄^{−1} does not occur, (C2) holds; (3) if σ(χ′) ≄ χ ⊗ κ̄ for all characters χ, χ′ of Γ_F on (𝔤^der)^{ss} and σ ∈ Aut(k), then (C3) and (C4) hold ((3) depends only on ρ̄_T).
items.note: Proof: Ad(exp X)(Y) = Σ ad(X)^i(Y)/i! for p ≫_G 0; U(ρ̄) is the p-Sylow of Gal(K/F); Lemma A.4. Improves Ray's Borel-valued GSp_{2g} lifting [Ray18].

items.name: Proposition B.1: Borel subgroups over a base are Zariski-locally conjugate
items.statement: [Con14, Corollary 5.2.13]: for any O-algebra A, two Borel subgroups B_1, B_2 of G_A are G-conjugate Zariski-locally on Spec A, and N_G(T_0)-conjugate if both contain T_0; N_G(B) = B over any base [Con14, Corollary 5.2.8].
items.note: Tau Ceti's ReductiveGroups roadmap plans Borel subgroups and their conjugacy (Layer 7) and the relative theory over a base (Layer 8).

items.name: The canonical torus T_G and the character χ_λ
items.statement: T_G = B/R_u(B) for any Borel B ⊂ G, canonically independent of B (G(O)-conjugacy and N_G(B) = B); fix B_0 ⊃ T_0 and identify T_G ×_O A with B_0/R_u(B_0) ×_O A. For v | p and cocharacters λ_τ : 𝔾_m → T_G (τ ∈ Hom_{ℚ_p}(F_v, E)), χ_λ : I_{F_v} → T_G(O) is χ_λ(σ) = ∏_τ λ_τ(τ(rec_v^{−1}(σ))), rec_v taking uniformisers to geometric Frobenii; λ dominant regular gives a p-adic Hodge type v_λ.

items.name: Definition B.2: F′_v-ordinary of weight λ
items.statement: Let A be a finite local E-algebra, F′_v/F_v finite and ρ : Γ_{F_v} → G(A) continuous. ρ is F′_v-ordinary of weight λ if there is a Borel B ⊂ G_A with ρ(Γ_{F_v}) ⊂ B(A) such that, for g ∈ G(A) with gBg^{−1} = B_0, the composite Γ_{F_v} → B(A) → B_0(A) → T_G(A) equals χ_λ on I_{F′_v} (independent of g).
items.note: The G-valued generalisation of ordinarity; LocalGaloisDeformationRings L8 plans ordinary flags for GL_n (ACC+ §6.2.6).

items.name: Bellovin–Gee: G-valued potentially semistable deformation rings (Theorem A)
items.statement: [BG19, Theorem A]: the quotient R^{□,v_λ}_ρ̄ of R^□_ρ̄ whose points in finite local E-algebras are the lifts potentially semistable over F′_v of p-adic Hodge type v_λ is equidimensional, every irreducible component of R^{□,v_λ}_ρ̄[1/p] has dimension dim G + [F_v : ℚ_p] dim Fl_G, and it has an open dense regular subscheme.
items.note: Kisin's GL_n theorem is planned (R08.3, L7 'the Kisin dimension formula'); the G-valued form is not. Routed as a source of L7.

items.name: Lemma B.3: the ordinary flag functor is closed
items.statement: Let 𝒢 ⊂ Fl_G (on R^{□,v_λ}_ρ̄-algebras) be the Borels fixed by ρ^λ_A(Γ_{F_v}) (closed; ρ^λ_A factors through B(A) for B ∈ 𝒢(A)), and 𝒢_λ ⊂ 𝒢 the B such that, Zariski-locally with gBg^{−1} = B_0, the projection of gρ^λ(σ)g^{−1} to T_G equals χ_λ(σ) for σ ∈ I_{F′_v}. Then 𝒢_λ is representable by a closed subscheme of 𝒢.
items.note: The ideal is generated by c_{β,σ} with c_{β,σ}X_β = p_β(Ad(gρ^λ(σ)g^{−1})X_β) − β(χ_λ(σ))X_β for positive β, independent of g, so it descends.

items.name: The ordinary quotient R^{△λ}_ρ̄
items.statement: R^{△λ}_ρ̄ is the scheme-theoretic image of 𝒢_λ[1/p] → Spec R^{□,v_λ}_ρ̄. Λ : 𝒢_λ → Spec R^{□,v_λ}_ρ̄ is proper, so Spec R^{△λ}_ρ̄[1/p] is its image; closed points lift uniquely (λ regular); on completed local rings (R^{□,v_λ}_ρ̄[1/p])^∧_y ↠ (R^{△λ}_ρ̄[1/p])^∧_y ↪ O^∧_{𝒢_λ[1/p],ỹ}, the last pro-representing pairs (ρ, B), which forms a subfunctor, hence the map is surjective.
items.note: Following Geraghty [Ger19] in the GL_n case.

items.name: Lemma B.4(1): the point criterion for ordinarity
items.statement: Let A be a finite local E-algebra and f : R^{□,v_λ}_ρ̄ → A an O-algebra map. Then f factors through R^{△λ}_ρ̄ iff f∘ρ^λ is F′_v-ordinary of weight λ (Definition B.2).
items.note: cf. [Ger19, Lemma 3.10].

items.name: Lemma B.4(2)–(3): the ordinary locus is a union of components
items.statement: R^{△λ}_ρ̄ is a union of irreducible components of R^{□,v_λ}_ρ̄; so R^{△λ}_ρ̄[1/p] has an open dense regular subscheme and all its components have dimension dim G + [F_v : ℚ_p] dim Fl_G. With a fixed multiplier μ : Γ_{F_v} → G/G^der(O), the same holds with dim G^der in place of dim G.
items.note: Proof: at y, O^∧_{𝒢_λ[1/p],ỹ} ≅ E[[X_1, …, X_h]]/(f_1, …, f_{h′}) with h ≥ dim G + dim Fl_G[F_v : ℚ_p] + h²(Γ_{F_v}, r(𝔟_0)) and h′ = h²(Γ_{F_v}, r(𝔟_0)), from the tangent space ker(Z¹(Γ_{F_v}, r(𝔟_0)) → Z¹(I_{F′_v}, r(𝔟_0/𝔫_0))), local Euler characteristic and H²(Γ_{F_v}, r(𝔟_0/𝔫_0)) = 0 (as [Ger19, Cor. 3.6, Lemma 3.7]); semistability is automatic ([Nek93, Prop. 1.28], [Pat16, Lemma 4.8]). The extraction of Boxer–Calegari–Gee already routed this lemma to L7. Misprints on p. 55 (source issues E6, E7).
